headline: Mercado Atlas faces a 12-month critical path on search relevance lift and observability cost reduction, with a Q3 decision that hinges on semantic search capability and 30% vendor consolidation savings.

sections.heading: Strategic Context
bullets: Board mandate is 30% observability cost reduction ahead of September 1 Datadog renewal; annual Datadog spend is $6M.
Marketplace conversion flat for 4 quarters; Lucia and Diego see semantic search as the primary lever to unlock a 2% uplift.
Dual search stack (Solr legacy + Elasticsearch newer) must consolidate to one platform with native vector support; Solr EOL is imminent.
Decision window is Q3 2026; Lucia sponsors, CTO signs, Diego is technical champion, Architecture Council reviews.

sections.heading: Recent Signals
bullets: Earnings reports highlight growth in Mercado Atlas Pay and credit portfolio expansion, creating higher volumes for both search and observability telemetry.
Engineering blog documents heavy Kafka and Flink infrastructure, indicating complex event-driven workloads that observability platform must handle at scale.
Procurement formally triggered vendor consolidation inquiry, signaling finance pressure and appetite for migration discussions.

sections.heading: Pain Points to Validate
bullets: Search latency p99 must drop to under 80ms at 10x current QPS; Diego flagged dense vector ingest throughput as a bottleneck risk.
ELSER quality and accuracy at Mercado Atlas's catalog scale is unproven; Diego needs confidence before committing to semantic pilot.
Cross-region replication latency between Sao Paulo and Buenos Aires is a blocker for firehose ingest replication; Elastic 8.13 improvements need benchmark validation.
Datadog cost per GB is unsustainable; Elastic's observability ingest pricing and compression efficiency are direct TCO levers.

sections.heading: Discovery Questions
bullets: How many SKUs are in the Mercado Atlas product catalog, and what is the current ELSER embedding batch size and latency per document?
What is the weekly search QPS peak on marketplace search today, and what is the 10x target (is that for regional sharding or global)?
On the observability side, what is the current daily ingest volume in GB, breakdown by logs vs metrics, and what compression ratio would meet the 30% cost target?
Diego mentioned cross-region replication latency; is the Sao Paulo cluster active-active or replication-only? What is today's P99 latency?
Are there security or compliance requirements that would gate adoption of ELSER (data residency, model transparency)?

sections.heading: Talking Points
bullets: Elastic's semantic search via ELSER is built-in and free across all tiers (Cloud and self-managed); no third-party embedding service cost. Datadog's equivalent requires custom LLM integration or partner APIs, adding operational overhead and recurring fees.

Vector search with HNSW is GA and optimized for ingest throughput; Mercado Atlas can run a proof-of-concept on a subset of Mercado Atlas Pay transaction search or product catalog without infrastructure changes.
Consolidation of Solr + Elasticsearch onto one platform reduces ops toil, licensing, and knowledge fragmentation; Elastic can handle both legacy keyword and modern semantic workloads natively.

Observability cost model: migrate Datadog logs and metrics to Elastic, apply ILM and tiering strategies (hot/warm/cold), and achieve 30%+ savings. Provide a side-by-side cost projection before September renewal to lock board confidence.
Cross-region replication: Elastic 8.13+ provides sub-100ms P99 latency for Sao Paulo to Buenos Aires geo pairs; share public benchmark and offer a geo-failover test in their AWS/GCP footprint.

sections.heading: Risks & Open Questions
bullets: Diego has not yet seen ELSER performance on Mercado Atlas's specific catalog; recommend a 72-hour POC on a product subset (e.g., Mercado Atlas Pay category) with HNSW vector ingest to de-risk the 2% conversion uplift claim.
Datadog renewal date is September 1; this is a hard stop for board decision. Confirm Lucia's timeline and whether CTO needs a comparative cost model by June 1 to allow vendor legal review.
No mention of real-time monitoring or alerting strategy post-migration; ensure Diego has input on Elastic's alerting and anomaly detection parity with Datadog before committing to full suite.
Security roadmap (entity analytics, attack surface management) was deferred by Diego; flag for future session, but do not block search + observability decision.

sections.heading: Pre-Meeting Prep
bullets: Have ELSER benchmark deck and cross-region replication benchmark (8.13) ready to screen-share or email immediately post-call.
Prepare a 30-minute observability cost model template with Mercado Atlas's $6M Datadog baseline and tiered Elasticsearch scenarios (Cloud Standard, Cloud Enterprise, self-managed).
Confirm which Elastic tier (Cloud or self-managed) aligns with Mercado Atlas's AWS/GCP multi-cloud strategy and procurement procurement appetite (likely Cloud for faster time-to-value).
Bring a one-pager on Solr migration tooling and timeline; offer architecture review session with Diego and his team if needed.
